candidates.label: BPL
candidates.definition_scope: Total binary languages; halting randomized O(log n)-space machines with bounded error on every input.
candidates.selection_judgment: Adds a central derandomization axis with no faithful current endpoint.
candidates.caveat: Keep halting/expected-time conventions explicit; this proposal is not a full new-pair baseline audit.

candidates.label: UL
candidates.definition_scope: Total languages accepted by O(log n)-space nondeterministic machines with at most one accepting computation on every input.
candidates.caveat: NL/poly=UL/poly is already known and does not settle NL=UL.

candidates.label: ∃R
candidates.definition_scope: Polynomial-time many-one closure of finite encodings of existential real formulas, using integer/rational constants.
candidates.selection_judgment: Adds a substantial computational geometry and real-algebra family within ordinary decision languages.
candidates.caveat: Not arbitrary-real-input BSS NP_R. Do not replace exact real feasibility by approximate or promise feasibility.

candidates.label: PL
candidates.definition_scope: Polynomial-time logspace probabilistic machines with unbounded-error acceptance, equivalently positive GapL.
candidates.selection_judgment: A compact representative of determinant/linear-algebra complexity, currently absent.
candidates.caveat: CeqL and parityL are alternative representatives, not aliases. No broad new-edge audit performed.

candidates.label: S₂P
candidates.definition_scope: Polynomial-time predicate with polynomial yes-witness defeating every no-witness and no-witness defeating every yes-witness, according to input membership.
candidates.selection_judgment: Represents a standard strengthened PH-collapse target and symmetric proof systems.
candidates.caveat: Self-complementary. Keep total-language decision version distinct from finding winning witnesses.

candidates.label: DLOGTIME-uniform NC¹
candidates.definition_scope: Polynomial-size logarithmic-depth bounded-fan-in circuits with a specified DLOGTIME uniformity convention.
candidates.selection_judgment: Exposes exact uniform parallelism below logspace without sacrificing nonuniform formula questions.
candidates.caveat: Do not silently replace current nonuniform NC1. Equality uNC1=L would already imply scored L⊆nonuniformNC1; a uniform-only separation need not.

candidates.label: DP
candidates.definition_scope: Languages L1∩L2 with L1∈NP and L2∈coNP.
candidates.selection_judgment: Expert-familiar home for exact optimization; compelling if Boolean-hierarchy collapse is a target family.
candidates.caveat: DP is not NP∩coNP. The first listed comparison also requires a coDP endpoint or an explicit complement-question mechanism.

candidates.label: RL
candidates.definition_scope: Halting randomized logarithmic space with one-sided error.
candidates.selection_judgment: Captures partial derandomization that BPL alone misses.
candidates.caveat: Do not assume L=RL iff L=BPL; choose error convention explicitly.

candidates.label: one-sided RNC
candidates.definition_scope: Uniform polynomial-size polylog-depth randomized circuits, one-sided error on all inputs.
candidates.selection_judgment: Adds parallel derandomization independently of sequential BPP.
candidates.caveat: Some literature uses RNC differently. A two-sided variant should use an explicit label such as BPNC, and should not be inferred equal.

candidates.label: CC
candidates.definition_scope: AC0 many-one closure of comparator-circuit value; equivalently the suitably uniform comparator-circuit class.
candidates.selection_judgment: Adds a distinct sub-P branch tied to stable marriage and lexicographic maximal matching.
candidates.caveat: Lower priority than BPL/UL/ExistsR for this50-slot benchmark; not CC0 modular circuits.

candidates.label: CL
candidates.definition_scope: Logarithmic clean workspace with polynomial catalytic workspace restored exactly for every initial catalyst content.
candidates.selection_judgment: Recent results make catalytic computation a serious alternative space resource.
candidates.caveat: CNL and randomized catalytic logspace are known to coincide with CL; do not add duplicate names. Full current-class relationships need separate audit.

candidates.label: EXP^NP
candidates.definition_scope: Deterministic exponential time with an ordinary NP oracle, with query length charged to runtime.
candidates.selection_judgment: Would expose a circuit lower-bound frontier above NEXP not settled by existing NEXP/Ppoly rows.
candidates.caveat: Use EXP^NP, not NP^EXP; do not transfer results with a promise-MA oracle or advice. Author2012 discussion explicitly gives linear-exponential NP-oracle version as open.

candidates.label: coNE
candidates.selection_judgment: Directly represents Asser’s spectrum complement problem.
candidates.caveat: Its separation already implies NP≠coNP and P≠NP. Its equality need not settle those. The binary spectrum theorem uses NE, not NEXP.

candidates.label: coNEXP
candidates.selection_judgment: Direct higher-time complementation endpoint, but adds complement multiplicity.
candidates.caveat: Do not conflate with coNE or cite the binary-spectrum equivalence for NEXP. Full importance case is weaker than for the highest-priority adds.

candidates.label: C=L
candidates.selection_judgment: Integer-matrix singularity gives a natural complete problem.
candidates.caveat: Complement question needs both endpoints; PL and CeqL are distinct candidates.

candidates.label: ⊕L
candidates.definition_scope: Parity of accepting polynomial-time nondeterministic logarithmic-space computations.
candidates.selection_judgment: Adds finite-field linear algebra, with strong exact-counting distinctions.
candidates.caveat: Do not add as another counting name without identifying the extra target family.

candidates.label: S₂E
representative_questions: Near-maximum circuit lower bounds at lower uniform complexity
candidates.selection_judgment: Valuable frontier reference, but its ordinary P/poly separation is already known.
candidates.caveat: A quantitative improvement to a known separation earns no pair point. Adding a known-hard class does not repair that mismatch.

candidates.label: MAEXP
candidates.definition_scope: Exponential-time Merlin–Arthur total-language class with explicit witness/randomness bounds.
candidates.selection_judgment: Useful boundary between known general-circuit lower bounds and NEXP.
candidates.caveat: Recent cited AMEXP/advice and E^promiseMA/1 theorems are not plain MAEXP theorems.

candidates.label: modular-only CC⁰
candidates.definition_scope: Polynomial-size constant-depth circuits whose internal gates are MOD_m for fixed m.
candidates.selection_judgment: A real restricted-circuit frontier, but too specialized to displace the three highest-priority adds.
candidates.caveat: Distinct from comparator CC and from ACC0. A scored AC0 source endpoint would matter if this target were admitted.

reasons.Sigma2P: Alternating quantifiers, natural minimization/completeness problems, and Karp–Lipton targets. Retain at least one second alternating level.
reasons.Delta2P: Adaptive polynomial-time access to NP; not interchangeable with nondeterministic alternation.
reasons.Theta2P: Nonadaptive polynomially many NP queries or logarithmically many adaptive queries. Δ₂P⊆Θ₂P asks whether adaptivity can be removed, and Θ₂P has natural exact-ranking problems.
reasons.PH: The whole hierarchy is needed for counting, quantum and real-feasibility comparisons and finite-level collapse questions.
reasons.Pi2P: Not an alias of Σ₂P. Many questions mirror Σ₂P after complementing both endpoints. Σ₂P=Π₂P implies PH=Σ₂P; inequality implies separation from the self-complementary Δ₂P.
reasons.S2P: A self-complementary symmetric-alternation refinement and stronger collapse target. Adding it while retaining every current related endpoint allocates eight slots to this block.

ph_allocation.recommendation: Retain Θ₂P before adding S₂P if the goal is preserving the current oracle-query dimension. If buying S₂P or another absent resource, consider demoting Π₂P before Θ₂P, while retaining Π₂P as background. Neither is mathematically redundant.

single_demotion_scenario_test.method: For each old unresolved ordered pair incident to C, separately assume inclusion and separation, saturate Benchmark.closure, and ask whether any resolved old candidate has neither endpoint C. Background inference retains every original class.
single_demotion_scenario_test.interpretation: A nonzero remaining point is not equal scientific fidelity or equal weighting. Tests are single demotions; simultaneous removals and new endpoints need separate checks. Only encoded ordinary implications are counted; independence is excluded and cannot be propagated as an ordinary edge.
